newsitem.title: USA: Nordstrom problems could run into new year.
newsitem.headline: Nordstrom problems could run into new year.

text.p: Nordstrom Inc.'s efforts to find the right formula for presenting merchandise will probably continue to hurt sales at the upscale clothing retailer well into 1997, analysts said Monday.

Throughout much of 1996, Seattle-based Nordstrom has been switching clothes among departments to match products more closely to niche customers. For instance, Nordstrom moved DKNY women's clothes from "Savvy," which targets progressive shoppers, to "Individualist," which is more contemporary.
But the short-term result has been confusion among Nordstrom staff and its loyal customers.

Shifts like that in other women's departments have caused a buildup of inventory as shoppers became frustrated at not finding clothes where they once were. Moreover, Nordstrom employees who buy the clothes from manufacturers are on a steep curve when learning about their new target customers.
A relatively solid third-quarter earnings report in November had raised expectations that Nordstrom might have recovered, but a near-term rebound is now unlikely, analysts said.
"I think you could see it within the next six months," said Jennifer Black Groves, an analyst at Portland, Ore.-based brokerage Black & Co.

Late Friday, Nordstrom said holiday sales would decline from last year's levels and cause earnings to fall below analysts' estimates. In a statement, Executive Vice President John Goesling attributed the decline "in part" to the fewer shopping days between Thanksgiving and Christmas this year.
But analysts blamed the sales shortfall on the product shift.
"They are still working on apparel assortments and that is what dragged down store performance," said Laura Richardson at Pacific Crest Securities, also based in Portland, Ore.
A Nordstrom spokeswoman Monday declined to comment further on fourth-quarter sales and the product realignment.

Analysts on average expect the company to earn 80 cents a share in its fiscal fourth quarter ending Jan. 31, according to the First Call service. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 1996, Nordstrom earned 67 cents a share, or $54 million in net income.
On Monday, several analysts lowered estimates, including Groves, who cut her fourth-quarter prediction to 70 cents a share.
By mid-year 1997, however, all the excess inventory should be sold and employees trained in the new system, putting Nordstrom on track for sales growth, analysts said.
They said a recent launch of clothes from designer Tommy Hilfiger has been very successful, and the company is moving to find new designers for some of its private-label clothes.
In addition, holiday sales in departments like men's apparel, shoes and fine jewelry are showing signs of strength.
Analysts also said the snowstorms and freezing rain that blanketed the Pacific Northwest, where Nordstrom has many stores, slightly hurt Christmas sales.
Nordstrom dropped $1.375 to $36.125 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq.
